chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said:
The divorced woman inherits and is inherited from until she sees the third blood. So when she sees it, then it is cut off.

key_terms.الدَّمَ الثَّالِثَ: The third blood (referring to the third menstrual period)
key_terms.الْمُطَلَّقَةُ: The divorced woman (specifically in the context of revocable divorce)
key_terms.انْقَطَعَ: It is cut off / severed (referring to the legal bond of inheritance)
key_terms.وَتُورَثُ: And she is inherited from (by her husband)

ai.seo_question: When does a divorced woman's waiting period end and her inheritance rights cease according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal status of a woman in the 'iddah of a revocable divorce (talaq raj'i), establishing that the marital bond and mutual inheritance rights persist until the third menstrual period is observed. This criterion aligns with the majority Shia view that the completion of three purity cycles (or menstruations) finalizes the transition toward irrevocability, distinguishing it from the waiting period of widowhood. The ruling underscores the continuity of financial ties during this transitional phase, ensuring the wife's security until the divorce is fully consummated.
